c.tagline: City of peace and okonomiyaki, gateway to the floating torii of Miyajima.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered, plentiful, and fairly pricey; ride-hailing is limited — GO and DiDi dispatch licensed taxis rather than private cars, and Uber in Japan also only books regular taxis.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police and 119 reaches fire and ambulance; English support is limited, so the Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787) offers 24/7 multilingual help.

hood_landmark.Peace Memorial Park (Naka): Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park A-Bomb Dome

avoid.reason: The Nagarekawa nightlife district has touts and pushy bars late at night; otherwise usual city awareness suffices.

hood_desc: The commercial heart of the city around the covered Hondori arcade and Kamiyacho, packed with department stores, restaurants, and the main streetcar interchange; the most convenient walkable base for first-timers.

The riverside civic core around the Peace Memorial Park, the A-Bomb Dome, and the Peace Memorial Museum, with wide boulevards and Hiroshima Castle nearby; best for travelers who want the must-see sights on their doorstep.
Hiroshima's main entertainment district, a dense grid of izakayas, bars, clubs, and okonomiyaki joints that comes alive after dark; suits night owls and diners.
The area around Hiroshima Station and the Shinkansen, a fast-modernizing hub of hotels, the ekie shopping complex, and easy connections; convenient for arrivals and day-trippers.
The sacred island of Itsukushima across the bay, home to the floating torii gate, mountain hikes, and roaming deer; a tranquil, scenic overnight escape from the city.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Japan.

transit.hours: Hiroden streetcars and city buses run from around 5:30 AM to about 11:00 PM; the Astram Line keeps similar hours, and there is no night service, so late trips fall to taxis.
transit.note: Hiroshima's signature transit is the Hiroden streetcar (tram) network — one of Japan's largest surviving tram systems — backed by an extensive city bus network, the elevated Astram Line people-mover, JR local trains, and ferries across the bay to Miyajima.
transit.pay: Tap a nationwide IC card (ICOCA, Suica, or Hiroshima's own MOBIRY DAYS) or a contactless credit card on trams and buses; a flat streetcar ride in the city is about ¥190 (~US$1.30). Cash and paper tickets are also accepted onboard.

transit.m: Airport Limousine Bus to Hiroshima Station (~50 min)
Airport Limousine Bus to Hiroshima Bus Center / Peace Park (~65 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can cause confusion; excellent service is standard and already included.
